newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MIDDLESBROUGH ABANDON BATTLE FOR POINTS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MIDDLESBROUGH ABANDON BATTLE FOR POINTS.

text.p: Middlesbrough Football Club have accepted the Premier League's decision to deduct the three points which ultimately cost the English side its place in the top flight last season, the club said in a statement on Friday.
The club lost the points and were fined 50,000 pounds ($81,400) after pulling out of a December match against Blackburn due to illness and injury to 23 players.
But while millionaire chairman Steve Gibson reluctantly accepted the penalty, he slammed league officials in an angry letter to league chief executive Peter Leaver.
Gibson said: "The attempts of my club to be heard and to receive a balanced and fair hearing have been met with a mixture of arrogance, complacency, incompetence, negligence and self-interest."
The club were critical of advice offered to them before the decision to postpone the game.

Gibson asked why league officials did not advise Middlesbrough that postponing a game when the club had more than 11 fit professionals could never constitute "just cause" when just three weeks later at a league commission hearing they were able to do so with such clarity.
Calling for an independent inquiry, Gibson said: "The extent of the penalties imposed defies natural justice and my football club can no longer be forgiving."
A Premier League spokesman confirmed they had received the letter.
"We will be responding in due course, but as far we are concerned the matter is closed and Middlesbrough ceased to be a member of the premier league at midnight on June 4," he said.

The club, which boast such international stars as Brazil's Juninho and Emerson as well as Italy's Fabrizio Ravanelli, received the support of Middlesbrough MP Stuart Bell who tabled a motion in Parliament on Thursday asking the league to appoint an independent body to review the case.
Middlesbrough suffered a roller-coaster season, ending up relegated but in two Wembley Cup finals, only to lose both.
